smugglerFlynn 2026/11/11 23:12
Replacing a good app is still extremely hard. Let me explain.

Commodities like todo apps and calculators rarely compete on features, they compete on product design. This includes look and feel, relation between elements, design choices on what exact common features are available.

All products are, at their essence, just a set of design decisions stitched and shipped together.

Now, making these design decisions is hard. It requires knowledge, consistency, and insights into how real people operate real products. Even as a sole user of the app you build you rarely know what you actually need.

LLMs are 'design-less' in their essence. Building your own todo app takes literal seconds and it all looks simple because LLMs will default most of these design decisions for you - until you try to use your new app daily and notice it somehow sucks. Building a good todo app or good calculator requires tweaking, publishing, polishing, and solving bugs, testing, rinse and repeat.

Another tricky side of this is that you might know logically what features you want, but you are not selecting one product over another logically. You need to try and see if that works for you, all the vibes and good parts and bad parts and design choices and colors, till you find something that "clicks" for you. Using pure Claude as a todo app only works as long as you want to have more Claude in your daily life.

In the meantime app store provides dozens of well-reviewed alternative solutions which look good and require zero maintenance.

And that's just a calculator or todo app. Non-commodity apps are even harder than that.

Design is dead (long live design)

I don't see any future where programs follow the static nature of old paradigm programming. A nice intuitive UI? What about just telling the app what I need when I need it? The gold standard of consumer UI is...another person.

If I have a team of god tier light speed SWE's at my disposal, why the fuck am I fumbling around in an actions panel? The program can just be dynamically modified in near real time to be whatever I need it to be in that moment.

If you extrapolate LLMs out to their extreme, you get a shape-shifting liquid array of bits in memory that manifest anything at the behest of a completely natural language interface.
